If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in late horizon (day 25–30) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (day 1–10) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast midpoint downward by 3–7% in mid-horizon (day 11–20) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 1–3% to forecast in late horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 1–3% from forecast in early horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast is below historical mean, increase forecast by 5–10% in mid-horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
